title: DR game day #1 follow-ups: close gaps found during Private restore drill (docs/timeouts/permissions)
creator: Rafael Mendes
description:
Context
- DR game day #1 (scenario: loss/corruption of control-plane DB) surfaced several operator-facing gaps and a couple of product/packaging papercuts that cost us time.
- This ticket tracks the follow-ups we agreed to close before we schedule game day #2 and before we invite the first pilot customer to run a restore drill with us.

Source material / links
- Confluence: Reliability initiative plan: sources/confluence/eng-sre/reliability-initiatives/private-dr-game-days-2025.json
- Confluence: Restore drill template: sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/game-days/private-restore-drill-template.json
- Drive notes/timeline: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/private-deployments/dr-game-day-1-notes-and-timeline.json
- SRE troubleshooting runbook (backup failures): sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/private-backup-failure-troubleshooting.json
- Incident thread during staged drill (permissions issue): sources/slack/incidents/1732639922.json

Goals (what “done” means)
1) The top time-sinks from game day #1 are addressed with either (a) product changes, or (b) explicit runbook steps + screenshots/examples.
2) The next drill can be executed by on-call + SE with minimal ad-hoc Slack guidance from Eng Private.
3) Pre-flight checks fail fast with actionable error messages (esp. object storage IAM/KMS).
4) Default timeouts/backoff are consistent with realistic data sizes (and called out in runbooks).

Discovered gaps + follow-ups (owners + deadlines)

A. Docs clarity / runbook structure
1) Make “restore to new cluster” vs “in-place restore” decision point explicit at top of both runbooks.
   - Problem observed: we spent ~20m debating which path matched the scenario.
   - Owner: Kira Thompson
   - Deadline: 2025-12-06
   - Deliverable: Updated Confluence runbooks with a one-page “Choose your restore path” section + small decision table.

2) Add a pre-restore checklist that includes required inputs (backup ID, storage target, KMS key ARN, cluster context, maintenance window).
   - Problem observed: missing KMS key + wrong kube context caused backtracking.
   - Owner: Elliot Price
   - Deadline: 2025-12-06
   - Deliverable: Checklist section added to runbooks; linked in incident-bot /restore-checklist.

3) Add explicit “expected output” snippets for the `rw-private-dr restore plan` step.
   - Problem observed: operators weren’t sure whether warnings were actionable.
   - Owner: Diego Santos
   - Deadline: 2025-12-10
   - Deliverable: Runbook snippets + clarify which warnings are safe to proceed vs must-fix.

B. Timeouts / performance assumptions
4) Increase and document default restore timeouts for large artifact bundles; ensure CLI surfaces progress.
   - Problem observed: restore exceeded the window largely due to conservative defaults + unclear progress.
   - Owner: Connor O'Brien
   - Deadline: 2025-12-13
   - Deliverable: Installer/CLI config defaults updated + release notes blurb; runbook includes sizing guidance.
   - Notes: please align with Helm values added for backup windows/timeouts (ref: sources/github/redwood-helm-charts/pr_452.json).

5) Add guidance for DB restore/PITR “how long will this take” and what levers exist (WAL archive location throughput, CPU/mem requests).
   - Problem observed: DB restore duration was a surprise; we didn’t have a good estimate model.
   - Owner: Michael Nguyen
   - Deadline: 2025-12-13
   - Deliverable: Runbook section + a short table of “data size -> expected time” from our drill numbers + caveats.

C. Permissions / IAM / KMS failure modes (highest friction)
6) Add a `rw-private-dr backup verify --check-permissions` mode that validates bucket access + KMS decrypt/encrypt + list/get/put on prefix.
   - Problem observed: we discovered AccessDenied mid-restore instead of failing fast.
   - Owner: Bruno Silva
   - Deadline: 2025-12-16
   - Deliverable: CLI flag + docs; include a least-privilege IAM policy example for S3+KMS.
   - References: sources/github/redwood-private-installer/pr_856.json, sources/github/redwood-terraform/pr_318.json.

7) Update Terraform examples to include a “break-glass restore role” pattern and clear separation between backup writer role and restore reader role.
   - Problem observed: we used an overly broad role during the drill; can’t recommend that to customers.
   - Owner: Bruno Silva
   - Deadline: 2025-12-20
   - Deliverable: Example updated + callouts about audit requirements.
   - References: sources/github/redwood-terraform/pr_327.json, sources/jira/internal-support/INT-932.json.

D. Operator ergonomics / safety rails
8) Add a single “maintenance mode is ON” verification command (and explain expected API behavior).
   - Problem observed: we toggled maintenance mode but had no single source of truth that it was enforced.
   - Owner: Ethan Park
   - Deadline: 2025-12-13
   - Deliverable: CLI/readout or API endpoint; runbook step shows what to look for.
   - References: ENG-4904, sources/slack/eng-platform/1732379055.json.

9) Add log locations + “what to attach” section for support/on-call handoff.
   - Problem observed: we lost ~15m re-collecting logs when escalating.
   - Owner: Rafael Mendes
   - Deadline: 2025-12-10
   - Deliverable: Runbook appendix listing relevant namespaces, pods, and commands; aligns with Support handoff work.
   - References: ENG-4920, sources/slack/eng-oncall/1732554301.json.

10) Observability: confirm alerts/dashboards cover last-successful backup age + restore drill annotation; ensure runbook links are correct.
   - Problem observed: dashboards existed but runbook links were stale/missing; alerts too noisy for paused clusters.
   - Owner: Sergio Costa
   - Deadline: 2025-12-16
   - Deliverable: Updated runbook link conventions + alert tuning doc note.
   - References: sources/github/observability-pack/pr_237.json, sources/slack/eng-sre/1732807711.json.

Proposed sub-issues to file (so we can track/close cleanly)
- ENG-4941: Add `--check-permissions` to rw-private-dr backup verify + IAM/KMS checks
- ENG-4942: Runbook updates: restore path decision table + pre-restore checklist
- ENG-4943: Default timeout changes + progress output for restore
- ENG-4944: Terraform example: break-glass restore role + least-privilege split
- ENG-4945: Observability runbook-link audit + paused-cluster alert suppression

Acceptance criteria
- All items A1–D10 are either shipped (code/docs) or explicitly waived with rationale in this ticket.
- We can run the drill following the runbooks without asking Eng Private for “tribal knowledge” steps.
- Pre-flight checks catch object storage/KMS issues before any destructive/invasive restore actions.

Open questions
- Do we want a formal RTO target per tier (standard vs strict) to drive timeout defaults, or keep defaults conservative and force operators to opt-in to larger windows?
- For air-gapped on-prem: should we add a dedicated section in the main runbooks, or link out to the air-gapped constraints doc only?

Updates / comments
